transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you lately that brought you here today?

Hi, yeah, thanks. Well, I came in mostly because I just feel worn out almost every day. It's like... even after a full night's sleep, my body and my head are still just dragging when I have to get up for my cashier shift. I just can't seem to shake this tired feeling.
Have you noticed a decrease in your interest or enjoyment in activities you used to like?

No, not really. I mean, I still like doing my usual stuff, like watching the game on weekends or just hanging out. I'm just... well, I'm usually pretty tired when I do them now. But the interest is definitely still there. I haven't lost that.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most of the time lately, even when you're not tired?
No, I wouldn't say I've been feeling down or depressed. I mean, it's really just the tiredness that's bothering me. My mood is generally fine, honestly. I don't feel sad or anything like that.
Do you feel like your sleep is refreshing, or do you often wake up still feeling tired?

No, it's really not refreshing at all. I usually get into bed feeling tired, but then... I just lie there. My mind starts going over things—like the bills, my work schedule, just thinking about whether everyone at home is okay. And even when I finally do fall asleep, I wake up feeling like I never really settled down. So yeah, I definitely wake up still feeling tired.
Do you have trouble falling asleep at the beginning of the night, or do you find yourself waking up multiple times during the night?

It's mostly at the beginning of the night. Yeah, just falling asleep is the hard part. Like I was saying, I just lie there for a long time thinking about everything. 

Once I'm actually out, I usually stay asleep. I don't really wake up a bunch of times in the middle of the night or anything like that. It's really just the getting to sleep part that takes forever, and then... well, waking up for my shift still feeling worn out.
When you're trying to fall asleep, are your thoughts usually racing or going over things repeatedly, making it hard for you to drift off?

Yeah, exactly. That's exactly it. My mind just won't shut off. It's like it's always jumping from one thing to the next. I'll be lying there thinking about money, and then I'm worrying about the relative we have staying with us right now. Then it's my wife, because she's been stressed lately, and then I'm thinking about my duties at church. And work... I just keep going over whether I'm messing up at my job as a cashier. It's just a constant loop of all these things, and it definitely keeps me from drifting off.
Do you find that you feel physically tense or mentally alert when you’re trying to fall asleep, like your body or mind is just not ready to rest even though you’re tired?

I don't think I feel physically tense, really. My muscles don't feel tight or anything like that. And I wouldn't say I feel alert, either. I'm usually pretty exhausted from standing at the register all day. So my body is definitely tired and ready to rest... it's really just my brain that won't shut up.
Do you find that your fatigue during the day affects your ability to perform tasks at work or home, like difficulty concentrating or staying motivated, even if you're not feeling down?

Yeah, it definitely affects my concentration. At work, I can be standing right at the register, looking directly at the screen, and I just... I still lose track of what I'm doing. My mind is off thinking about things at home or worrying about the bills. And that's when I end up having to recount the drawer or catch a small mistake I made. So, yeah, it definitely makes it harder to focus on the job.
How often do you have trouble falling asleep like this, and have these sleep difficulties been happening almost every night for at least a month or more?

Yeah, it's most nights. It's definitely been happening for more than a month now. I mean, I get in bed tired, but then I just lie there going over the bills, my work schedule, and worrying about whether everyone at home is okay. And honestly, even when I do finally get to sleep, I wake up the next morning feeling like I never really settled down at all.
Do you ever notice that your heart races, you feel restless, or you just can't seem to relax even when you're trying to wind down for bed?

No, my heart doesn't really race or anything like that. Like I mentioned earlier, my body is usually just exhausted from being on my feet at work all day. I don't really get restless... I mean, I mostly just lay there still, trying to sleep. It's really just my thoughts that won't stop, not my body.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about things like work, family, or other responsibilities even during the day when you're not trying to sleep?

Yeah, pretty much all day. It feels like my mind is always jumping from one thing to the next. I'll be worrying about money, then I'm thinking about the relative staying with us right now, or how stressed my wife is. And then I start thinking about my church duties, or wondering if I'm messing up at work. It just doesn't really stop, even when I'm busy.
Do you feel that your main problem is not being able to sleep well, and that this is the primary source of your fatigue and difficulty during the day?

I don't think so, no. I mean, the sleep thing is definitely frustrating, but... even if I did sleep well, I think I'd still be tired, you know? It's just... the constant worrying all day that really wears me out. The sleep issues just make it a little harder, but the worrying is the main thing.
Do you feel that your constant worrying affects your ability to function in areas of your life beyond just sleep, like at work, with your family, or in your daily responsibilities?

Yeah, it does. Like at work, I've noticed I'm making these small mistakes because my mind is somewhere else, so I've had to start double-checking my cash drawer a lot more often just to be safe. And with my other responsibilities... I've actually cut back on volunteering at the food pantry lately. I just don't feel like I can keep up with everything right now.
